“Experience is not a veil that shuts man off from nature; it…” — John Dewey (Experience and Nature)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Experience and Nature. Theme: experience.

English

Experience is not a veil that shuts man off from nature; it is a means of penetrating continually further into the heart of nature.

About John Dewey

John Dewey (1859–1952) was the leading American pragmatist of the progressive era, joining philosophy to experimental education and democratic reform. Educated at Vermont and Johns Hopkins, he taught at Michigan, Chicago—where he ran the Laboratory School—and Columbia.

How to read this passage

Empiricists treat experience as the source of ideas; phenomenologists describe its structure; pragmatists treat it as experimental and revisable. This passage enters that discussion through experience, nature, inquiry.

Concepts in this quote

Experience
Experience is the lived encounter with world and self—foundation or limit for knowledge, art, and ethics.
Nature
Philosophy quotes about nature ask what the cosmos is, how humans belong in it, and whether “natural” can guide ethics or politics.
Inquiry
Inquiry is the disciplined pursuit of better questions and answers—philosophy as method rather than dogma.
